```{r setup}
library(Lynch)
library(ggplot2)
```

Lynch has three kinds of palette. Pick the kind that matches your data:

| Kind | For | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete | categories | `lynch_palettes` |
| Sequential | ordered values, low to high | `lynch_sequential` |
| Diverging | values either side of a midpoint | `lynch_diverging` |

## Picking colours

`lynch_palette()` returns a palette by name. Printing it draws the colours.

```{r, fig.height = 1.2}
lynch_palette("twin_peaks")
```

Ask for fewer colours with `n`. Discrete palettes have five colours, so `n` can be at most five.

```{r, fig.height = 1.2}
lynch_palette("blue_velvet", 3)
```

Sequential and diverging ramps are interpolated, so they give any number of colours.

```{r, fig.height = 1.2}
lynch_palette("dune", 12, type = "sequential")
lynch_palette("mulholland_drive", type = "diverging")
```

The result keeps a `palette` class for printing. Use `unclass()` when you want a plain character vector.

```{r}
unclass(lynch_palette("wild_at_heart"))
```

## Discrete palettes

There are six film palettes and five colour-blind-safe versions.

```{r}
names(lynch_palettes)
```

Use `scale_colour_lynch_d()` or `scale_fill_lynch_d()` for categories.

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_lynch_d("lost_highway") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Reverse the order with `direction = -1`. If the data has more categories than the palette has colours, the extra levels are drawn as `NA` and you get a warning.

## Colour blindness

Every film palette keeps its colours distinct with red-green colour blindness except `blue_velvet`. `blue_velvet_safe` keeps the four of its colours that do. `lynch_accessibility` has the test results.

```{r}
lynch_accessibility[, c("palette", "n_colours", "deutan", "protan", "rating")]
```

Any palette but `blue_velvet` works for up to five groups. For Blue Velvet, use `blue_velvet_safe` with four groups or fewer.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_lynch_d("twin_peaks", name = "Cylinders") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Sequential and diverging scales

`scale_colour_lynch_c()` and `scale_fill_lynch_c()` map numbers to a ramp. The default is sequential.

```{r}
ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_lynch_c("dune") +
  theme_minimal()
```

For values either side of a reference point, use `type = "diverging"` and set `midpoint`. Without a midpoint, the grey centre sits halfway across the data range.

```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  year = 2001:2020,
  change = c(-4, -3, -3, -1, 0, 1, -2, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5, 3, 6, 8, 7, 9, 12, 10, 14)
)

ggplot(df, aes(year, change, fill = change)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_lynch_c("mulholland_drive", type = "diverging", midpoint = 0) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Only four films have diverging ramps:

```{r}
names(lynch_diverging)
```

## Base graphics

The palettes are plain colour vectors, so they work anywhere R takes colours.

```{r}
image(volcano, col = lynch_palette("mulholland_drive", 50, type = "sequential"), axes = FALSE)
```
